questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The companys latest report, B. which was released only this morning, C. provided the data that D. supports our initial hypothesis.

options.text: which was released only this morning

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the lack of a possessive apostrophe in the word "**companys**."
 
• To indicate that the report belongs to the company, the noun "company" must be in its possessive form.
 
• The correct spelling should be "**company's**" (singular possessive) to correctly modify the noun "report."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part A** (Option 1) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The **company's** latest report, which was released only this morning, provided the data that supports our initial hypothesis."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **B: "which was released only this morning," **– This is a correctly structured non-restrictive relative clause providing additional information.
 
• **C: "provided the data that"** – This part uses the past tense "provided" correctly to describe an action that has already occurred.
 
• **D: "supports our initial hypothesis."** – This part is grammatically correct; "supports" is in the present tense because it describes a fact that remains true.
 
• **Punctuation Rule:** Singular nouns almost always form the possessive by adding an apostrophe and an "s" (*'s*).

questions.question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The reason for his failure B. is because he C. didn't study D. for the exam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of "**is because**" following the phrase "**The reason**."
 
• In formal English, the word "reason" itself implies a cause, making the word "because" redundant (a grammatical error known as a pleonasm).
 
• The noun "reason" should be followed by a complement clause beginning with "**that**" rather than the conjunction "because."
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part B** (Option 2) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The reason for his failure **is that** he didn't study for the exam."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "The reason for his failure"** – This serves as the subject of the sentence and is grammatically sound.
 
• **C: "didn't study"** – This is the correct past tense negative form of the verb.
 
• **D: "for the exam."** – This prepositional phrase correctly completes the thought.
 
• **Redundancy Rule:** Avoid using "the reason is because" in professional or academic writing; instead, use "the reason is that" or restructure the sentence to start with "He failed because..."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: SURRENDER
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Yield**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

 
• The word **"Surrender"** means to give up or yield to the power, control, or possession of another, often by compulsion or demand. (आत्मसमर्पण करना)

 

 
• **Example: **The soldiers decided to surrender rather than face certain defeat.

 

 

 
• **"Yield"** is a synonym of surrender and means to give way to arguments, demands, or pressure. It also refers to relinquishing possession or control. (समर्पण करना)

 

 
• **Example: **After a long debate, she finally yielded to their suggestions.

 

 

 
• Hence, the most appropriate synonym of **'Surrender'** is **'Yield'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Yield**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Resist **(प्रतिरोध करना): To fight against or oppose something actively.

 

 
• **Example:** They resisted the changes proposed by the management.

 

 

 
• **Confront **(सामना करना): To face or deal with a difficult situation or person directly.

 

 
• **Example: **She had to confront her fears before she could move forward.

 

 

 
• **Oppose** (विरोध करना): To disapprove of and attempt to prevent, especially by argument.

 

 
• **Example:** The citizens opposed the construction of the new factory in their town.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the primary ethical dilemma posed by climate migration?

options.text: Whether migrants should be allowed to resettle
How the burden of climate migration should be shared
Whether climate change is a natural occurrence
How to prevent future climate change

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the passage:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states in the second paragraph: "It puts in sharp relief the hard question of how the burden is to be shared. A strong case, based on the issue of climate justice, places the main burden on the industrialised world."
 
• The text focuses on the ethical response required from industrialized nations because they are the largest historical producers of greenhouse gases. The central dilemma discussed is determining who is responsible for providing financial, logistical, and humanitarian support to those displaced by climate change.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **How the burden of climate migration should be shared.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Whether migrants should be allowed to resettle)**: Incorrect. The passage assumes resettlement is necessary and focuses instead on establishing "legal and safe channels of resettlement," not debating whether they should be allowed to do so.
 
• **Option 3 (Whether climate change is a natural occurrence)**: Incorrect. The passage treats climate change as a crisis heavily driven by the carbon-polluting industries of the industrialized world, not as a natural occurrence or a point of debate.
 
• **Option 4 (How to prevent future climate change)**: Incorrect. While mitigation is mentioned, the primary focus of the passage and the specific ethical dilemma it highlights is the immediate humanitarian crisis of forced migration and how to equitably manage and fund the response.

questions.question: in the passage, the word "vexing most nearly means:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What is meant by "climate justice as described in the passage?

options.text: Accountability of industrialized nations for climate damage
Global cooperation to reverse climate change

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing "climate justice" in the passage:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly links the concept of "climate justice" to the historical responsibility of wealthy nations. It states: "A strong case, based on the issue of climate justice, places the main burden on the industrialised world. They have been the biggest per-capita producers of greenhouse gases..."
 
• The text argues that because industrialized nations built their prosperity through carbon-polluting industries that are now destroying less-developed countries, an "ethical and equitable response" demands they provide the necessary financial and logistical assistance.
 
• Therefore, in this context, climate justice means holding the nations that caused the majority of the climate crisis accountable for repairing the damage and mitigating its effects.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Accountability of industrialized nations for climate damage.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Fair distribution of global resources)**: Incorrect because while resource distribution is a broad global issue, the passage specifically defines climate justice in terms of bearing the burden for historical greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• **Option 3 (Equity in migration policies)**: Incorrect because migration policy equity is discussed in the first paragraph as part of a multi-faceted strategy, but the term "climate justice" in the second paragraph is specifically applied to the accountability of industrialized nations for causing the crisis.
 
• **Option 4 (Global cooperation to reverse climate change)**: Incorrect because the passage primarily focuses on managing the humanitarian fallout (migration) and assigning responsibility for adaptation and resettlement, rather than reversing climate change itself.

questions.question: How does the passage characterize the current definition of "refugees" in the context of climate migration?

options.text: It is too broad to include climate migrants
It is narrow and insufficient to cover climate migrants
It is accurate and universally accepted
It is too rigid to address global migration

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the passage:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states that a thorough solution requires a "shift away from the present, limited definition of refugees."
 
• Earlier in the text, it notes that millions of displaced people currently "have no official legal status as 'climate refugees.'"
 
• This clearly indicates that the current legal definition is too "limited" (narrow) and therefore insufficient to provide official status and protection to people displaced specifically by climate change.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **It is narrow and insufficient to cover climate migrants.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (It is too broad to include climate migrants)**: Incorrect because the passage describes the definition as "limited," which is the opposite of broad. If it were too broad, climate migrants might already accidentally fall under it.
 
• **Option 3 (It is accurate and universally accepted)**: Incorrect because the author argues for the "creation of new international humanitarian and legal protocols" to replace or update it, indicating it is currently inadequate.
 
• **Option 4 (It is too rigid to address global migration)**: Incorrect because the passage's critique is specifically focused on its failure to cover *climate migrants*, making Option 2 the most precise and text-supported choice.

questions.question: What strategy is suggested in the passage to address climate migration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the passage:***

 
 
• The passage explicitly advocates for a strategy that is forward-looking. It states that a thorough solution "requires proactive, not reactive, policy."
 
• Furthermore, it highlights the need for a "serious investment in building climate resilience among those who are likely to be vulnerable, so that they are not displaced in the first place."
 
• This clearly points to a strategy focused on anticipating the problem and putting proactive measures in place to prevent populations from being uprooted.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Proactive measures to prevent displacement.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Reactive measures to control migration)**: Incorrect because the text explicitly states the policy should be "proactive, not reactive."
 
• **Option 3 (Total ban on climate migration)**: Incorrect because the author argues for the "establishment of legal and safe channels of resettlement," which is the opposite of a ban.
 
• **Option 4 (International immigration restrictions)**: Incorrect because the passage supports creating "new international humanitarian and legal protocols to acknowledge and safeguard climate migrants," rather than restricting them.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the word "board" with a different meaning from the others?

options.text: The board of directors met yesterday.
The captain had to board the ship.
He nailed a picture of the board of directors on the wall.
The board of directors decided to hire a new CEO.

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Bookworm** (पुस्तक प्रेमी / किताबों का कीड़ा): A person who enjoys reading books, often to the exclusion of other activities.

 

 
• **Example:** He’s such a bookworm that he prefers spending his weekends at the library.

 

 

 
• **Librarian** (पुस्तकालयाध्यक्ष): A person who works in or manages a library.

 

 
• **Example:** The librarian helped me find the book I was looking for.

 

 

 
• **Reader** (पाठक): A person who reads, especially someone who reads for pleasure or study.

 

 
• **Example:** She is an avid reader and finishes at least one book every week.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Esoteric
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Common**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Esoteric"** means something that is intended for or understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge or interest. (गूढ़, केवल कुछ लोगों के लिए समझने योग्य)

 
 
• **Example:** Quantum physics can be considered esoteric because its concepts are not easily understood by the general public.
 
 

 
• **"Common"** refers to something that is widespread, ordinary, or familiar to most people; it contrasts with something specialized or rare like "esoteric." (सामान्य)

 
 
• **Example:** Mobile phones have become so common that almost everyone owns one.
 
 

 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Esoteric' **is **'Common'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Common**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Arcane** (रहस्यमय): Something mysterious or understood by very few people.

 
 
• **Example:** The ancient script on the walls of the temple was arcane and undecipherable.
 
 

 
• **Mystical** (अलौकिक): Relating to spiritual or supernatural elements that are beyond ordinary understanding.

 
 
• **Example:** The mystical aura of the monastery left everyone mesmerized.
 
 

 
• **Obscure** (अस्पष्ट): Something unclear or hidden; not easily understood.

 
 
• **Example:** The poet used obscure references in his work that were difficult for the audience to grasp.

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The report could not be accessed without the proper security clearance.

options.text: They could not access the report without the proper security clearance.
The report cannot be accessed without the proper security clearance.
Without the proper security clearance, the report was not accessed.
The proper security clearance could not access the report.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Identify the Subject and Agent:** In the passive sentence "The report could not be accessed...", the agent (who is doing the accessing) is missing. In such cases, we use a general pronoun like **"They," "You,"** or **"One"** as the active subject.
 
• **Identify the Verb and Tense:** The verb is **"could not be accessed"** (Modal + be + V3). In the active voice, this becomes **"could not access"** (Modal + V1).
 
• **Rearrange the Sentence:** The placeholder subject "They" takes the action, "the report" becomes the direct object, and the conditional phrase "without the proper security clearance" remains at the end.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They could not access the report without the proper security clearance."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "cannot be accessed" – This changes the tense from the past possibility (could) to present (cannot) and remains in the passive voice.
 
• **Option 3:** "was not accessed" – This is still passive and changes the modal "could not" to a simple past statement of fact.
 
• **Option 4:** "The proper security clearance could not access..." – This is logically incorrect; a "clearance" is a status/document and cannot physically perform the action of accessing a report.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The director said, "The new actor will be arriving shortly."

options.text: The director said that the new actor would be arriving shortly.
The director said that the new actor will be arriving shortly.
The director said that the new actor would arrive shortly.
The director said that the new actor had been arriving shortly.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** The director said, "The new actor will be arriving shortly."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Modal Verb Change (Backshifting):**
 
 
• When the reporting verb is in the past ("said"), modal verbs in the direct speech must shift to their past forms.
 
• The modal **"will"** changes to **"would."**
 
 
 
• **Tense Maintenance (Continuous Aspect):**
 
 
• The original sentence is in the Future Continuous ("will be arriving").
 
• In indirect speech, the continuous aspect **"be arriving"** is preserved after the shifted modal **"would."**
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The comma and quotation marks are removed and replaced by **"that"** to connect the reporting clause with the reported statement.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The director said that the new actor would be arriving shortly."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Fails to shift the modal "will" to "would," which is necessary when the reporting verb is in the past.
 
• **Option 3:** Changes the aspect from continuous ("be arriving") to simple ("arrive"), which alters the original meaning of the speaker.
 
• **Option 4:** Uses the past perfect continuous ("had been arriving"), which incorrectly implies a past habitual action rather than a future planned arrival.

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

Each of the girls **narrated their** story

options.text: Each of the girls narrated there story
Each of the girls narrated his story
Each of the girls narrated her story
Each of the girls narrated their stories

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Each of the girls narrated her story**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is "**Each of the girls**," which is singular.
 
• The corresponding pronoun that aligns with the singular subject is "**her**" because the sentence refers to "**girls**" (females).
 
• **Option 3** is the only grammatically correct choice that adheres to subject-pronoun agreement.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Each of the girls narrated **her**__ story."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "there story"** is incorrect because "there" is an adverb, not a possessive pronoun.
 
• **Option 2: "his story"** is incorrect because it does not align with the gender reference to "girls."
 
• **Option 4: "their stories"** is incorrect because it assumes plural narration, while the subject "Each" is singular.

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

My brother built this house in 2005.

options.text: This house was built by my brother in 2005.
This house is built by my brother in 2005.
This house built by my brother in 2005.
This house was being built by my brother in 2005.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Identify the Tense:** The active sentence "built" is in the **Simple Past Tense**.
 
• **Passive Structure for Simple Past:** The formula is **Object + was/were + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject**.
 
• **Step 1:** Identify the object "this house" and make it the new subject. Since "house" is singular, we use **"was."**
 
• **Step 2:** Use the third form (Past Participle) of the verb "build," which is **"built."**
 
• **Step 3:** Add the agent "by my brother" and the time reference "in 2005."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"This house was built by my brother in 2005."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "is built" – This is the Present Simple Passive. It is incorrect because the action happened in the past (2005).
 
• **Option 3:** "built" – This lacks the auxiliary verb "was," making it grammatically incomplete as a passive sentence.
 
• **Option 4:** "was being built" – This is the Past Continuous Passive. It suggests the building was an ongoing process at that specific time, rather than a completed action.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

The professor explained that although the theory had been considered correct for centuries, new findings now proved that it was flawed.

options.text: The professor explained, "Although the theory had been considered correct for centuries, new findings now prove that it is flawed."
The professor explained, "Although the theory was considered correct for centuries, new findings now prove that it is flawed."
The professor explained, "Although the theory has been considered correct for centuries, new findings now prove that it is flawed."
The professor explained, "Although the theory was considered correct for centuries, new findings then proved that it was flawed."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The professor explained that although the theory had been considered correct for centuries, new findings now proved that it was flawed.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Tense Change (Forward-shifting):**
 
 
• The past perfect passive **"had been considered"** shifts forward to the present perfect passive **"has been considered"** to show an action that started in the past and continues to the present moment of speaking.
 
• The simple past **"proved"** shifts forward to the simple present **"prove."**
 
• The simple past **"was"** shifts forward to the simple present **"is."**
 
 
 
• **Time Expressions:**
 
 
• The word **"now"** in the indirect speech suggests that at the time of the professor's original speech, the findings were current. Therefore, **"now"** is retained or restored in the direct speech.
 
 
 
• **Punctuation:**
 
 
• The conjunction "that" is removed and replaced with a comma and quotation marks to enclose the speaker's exact words.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The professor explained, 'Although the theory has been considered correct for centuries, new findings now prove that it is flawed.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Retains the past perfect ("had been considered"), which would imply the theory stopped being considered correct *before* another past event, rather than up until the moment of speaking.
 
• **Option 2:** Uses the simple past ("was considered"), which loses the "duration" aspect emphasized by "for centuries" in the original context.
 
• **Option 4:** Uses "then" and "proved" (past tense), which keeps the sentence in a reported/past perspective rather than converting it to the speaker's direct present perspective.

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. The old man, with his kind eyes and twisted hands, smiled softly.

Q. He had lived a whole life as a woodcarver, and his store was a museum of fragile works of art.

R. He held a tiny bird he was carving, his thumb caressing the slippery wood.

S. They all had a story, a memory, a piece of his soul.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph is a character-driven narrative that moves from a general introduction of the person to their history, then to a specific action, and finally to a thematic reflection.
 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** because it introduces the subject (the old man) and establishes his physical presence and mood:
 
 
• "The old man, with his kind eyes and twisted hands, smiled softly."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows** to provide context and background for the man, explaining his profession and the setting of the scene:
 
 
• "He had lived a whole life as a woodcarver, and his store was a museum of fragile works of art."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the third sentence** as it transitions from the general store to the specific piece he is working on at this moment:
 
 
• "He held a tiny bird he was carving, his thumb caressing the slippery wood."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the fourth sentence** because the pronoun "They" refers back to the "works of art" mentioned in Q (and includes the bird in R), providing a sentimental conclusion to the passage:
 
 
• "They all had a story, a memory, a piece of his soul."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQRS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"The old man, with his kind eyes and twisted hands, smiled softly. He had lived a whole life as a woodcarver, and his store was a museum of fragile works of art. He held a tiny bird he was carving, his thumb caressing the slippery wood. They all had a story, a memory, a piece of his soul."

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P: She examined the old manuscript closely, observing the fading ink..

Q: After that, she turned the fragile pages carefully so as not to break them any more.

R: With a long history filled with tales, the book has been handed down through the centuries.

S: Before starting the restoration procedure, she got the equipment and supplies she would need ready.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph follows a logical flow from the historical context of an object to the professional preparation and execution of its restoration.
 
• **Sentence R is the first sentence** as it introduces the subject (the book) and provides the necessary background information regarding its age and significance:
 
 
• "With a long history filled with tales, the book has been handed down through the centuries."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S follows** by shifting the focus to the restorer's preparation, setting the stage for the work to come:
 
 
• "Before starting the restoration procedure, she got the equipment and supplies she would need ready."
 
 
 
• **Sentence P is the third sentence** because it describes the first active step of the restoration process—the detailed visual inspection:
 
 
• "She examined the old manuscript closely, observing the fading ink."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q is the fourth** as it uses the transition phrase "After that" to indicate the next physical action taken after the initial examination:
 
 
• "After that, she turned the fragile pages carefully so as not to break them any more."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **RSPQ**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"With a long history filled with tales, the book has been handed down through the centuries. Before starting the restoration procedure, she got the equipment and supplies she would need ready. She examined the old manuscript closely, observing the fading ink. After that, she turned the fragile pages carefully so as not to break them any more."
